event.summary: Deleting the kind test also removes the completed-create reboot retry oracle
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: removing the terminal-kind reboot test also removes its still-valid check that retrying a successfully created session after a host reboot returns the original session, rather than creating a new one. This is lost regression protection, not a demonstrated current duplicate-create bug. Original c1 history preserved: terminal-kind/stream-kind fields really are retired in protocol 77, and their assertions should go; the old proposed_drop correctly refutes the misleading-kind concern, but does not justify deleting this independent identity oracle with them. Deleted parent create_idempotency.rs:329-382 creates an actual keyed session under boot-a, ends every terminal host, reloads under boot-b, asserts the existing session is Interrupted, retries the same key and requires replay.id == first.id. The retained same-boot restart fixture at reviewed :244-298 asserts ID equality and one actual host while the host survives; it does not test key survival through reboot conversion. The retained reboot fixture at :833-906 starts from a crashed never-launched Pending reservation and requires a launch, the opposite outcome. Store tests are not an equivalent replacement: store.rs:13540-13645 directly checks that an interrupted row with a recorded terminal address refuses a pending-launch takeover; it neither runs record_boot on a completed reservation nor exercises the retry caller after conversion. store.rs:10264-10312 and :10582-10655 verify boot conversion using unkeyed rows, not retention of a created key. core.rs:28519-28630 exercises a pending reservation that ended with ObservedExit and settlement, with no boot transaction. A regression that loses only Created reservations during reboot conversion would satisfy these remaining cases but fail the deleted same-ID assertion. Source correctness of resolve_reservation (:9884-9960) and replay_created_session (:10182-10240) does not supply the lost oracle. Contract at SPEC_impl.md:3535-3540: 'Every keyed create gets a session-lifetime reservation: app creates, agent `create`/`clone`, and spawn all retain the key until the created session is deleted.' The interrupted row still exists; a reboot is not Delete. SPEC.md:3813-3818 likewise says retry returns the existing child rather than creating another and keys live as long as that child does. Suggested fix: retain the completed-create/reboot/key-retry identity assertion while removing only obsolete kind fields; no retired tmux fixture is needed. Suggested bucket: other (test-only regression coverage). Confidence: confirmed source discrimination at the deletion revision, no execution. proposed_drop: false for the lost reboot identity oracle; earlier field-retirement rationale remains applicable only to obsolete field assertions. possible_cover: none in supplied neighbour context; no prohibited coverage sources searched. Could-be-highest: no established shipped security or loss-of-work route; duplicate creation is a hypothetical future regression detected by the removed test, not an observed product defect. Through-tip source search found no matching reboot replay test, and subsequent diffs of create_idempotency.rs and boot_id_durable_outcome.rs are empty; store.rs only changes comments. Final bounded caller/alternative checks continue before this discovery pass ends. No tests, builds or reproductions.
